title: Tooling: 2.25x faster corrected f(7) census with identical traversal
body:
The corrected PR2973 census scans its prefix sets to construct pair supports at every extension. This replaces those loops with two 64-bit permutations: compress each Hamming-weight parity coset separately, and keep its mask relative to the current walk position. A written invariant/rollback argument establishes the same traversal, both budgets, leaf coverage and ordered witnesses. The frozen engine is authenticated and adapted in a fresh workspace; predecessor files remain unchanged.

**Status: tooling improvement with a scoped representation-equivalence proof.** No new kappa, length 22 exclusion or supplier claim.

| Complete same-input replay | Original | Accelerated | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Six corrected L18/L20 cases, 917,753,852 nodes | 226.66 s | 100.52 s | 2.25x |

Every non-timing JSON field and witness file agrees. All six runs start at the empty prefix without a cap. Timing excludes compilation and additional controls; these are serial local Linux/GCC measurements, not a universal speed guarantee or multiplication-runtime claim. The earlier complete experiment measured 2.26x.

Verification passed:
- Registered Python 3.12 replay of controls and both complete engines.
- 164 inherited raw-product comparisons, 36 capped seven-source Python comparisons, and a new scalar oracle reconstructing internal sets and collision counts.
- All 448 permutation basis/label cases; sanitizer-trap builds; positive universal witnesses including the old wrong-budget counterexample; partial/multiple-shard controls.
- Four rejecting implementation mutants and two source/adapter invalidation controls, alongside the predecessor's 12 failure checks.
- Read-only Git-free optimized Python 3.14 export with identical control results; all 15 committed package/input files match tested bytes.

```sh
python3 -I -B research/f7-parity-mask-replay/verify.py --work /tmp/f7-mask-replay
```

Use a fresh output directory and a C11-capable `cc` with unsigned 128-bit integer and sanitizer-trap support. Expected: `PASS_F7_PARITY_MASK_CONTROLS` and `PASS_F7_PARITY_MASK_COMPLETE`. The registered hook splits these obligations into bounded commands. [Package, proof and receipts](https://github.com/tekuuu/integer-mult-bounds/tree/34d7c3feaf87b878d9524c215b678403b8afdc08/research/f7-parity-mask-replay).

The complete comparison shares the predecessor's DFS/pruning logic; it is not a second independent full-domain implementation proof. The retained result is still `22 <= f(7) <= 24` in the PR943 singleton prefix-walk model. Length22, native/supplier admission and the selected frontier are outside scope. Hosted CI and independent human/formal-kernel review are not claimed passed.

Scientific base `472f4e78b338215f0b2c3f590b0bc7d2f03c02eb`; synchronized submission base `b3f3ee0392b71b118fd086a6eaf6b4cab54ef455`; PR2973 source `d48f3945dbb1ef5d06835744c4082b3bd04181c0`. OS seed 88, verification engineering. [Canonical claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18977093). Fresh PR2978/2979 and active set-cover work concern different objects.

Credit Nicholas Stone for the corrected census and independent oracles, Ross Richardson for the PR943 model, Aaron Wang/opencode for the preceding census/set-cover work, and Douglas Colkitt's retained construction lineage. Tekalign (@tekuuu), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Apache-2.0.

Only `research/f7-parity-mask-replay/` is added: nine files, approximately 83 KB, with most lines in exact receipts. No shared tooling, frozen predecessor, `upstream/` or selected-frontier file changes.
